tasks.name: Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud.

topics.name: AWS Cloud Value Proposition & Global Reach
High Availability, Elasticity & Agility

selection_rules: Distinguish elasticity (dynamic automatic scaling to match load) from scalability (ability to accommodate growth).
Recognize agility as rapid innovation and instant provisioning compared to lengthy on-premises procurement.
Leverage AWS global infrastructure to deploy applications globally in minutes with minimal latency.
common_confusions: Confusing elasticity with high availability or fault tolerance.
Assuming agility refers to software sprint methodology rather than rapid resource provisioning.
Confusing global reach with multi-region active-active disaster recovery.

tasks.name: Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud.

topics.name: AWS Well-Architected Framework: 6 Pillars
Architectural Design Principles across Pillars

selection_rules: Recall the six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.
Apply foundational principles: stop guessing capacity needs, test systems at production scale, automate architectural experimentation.
Implement evolutionary architectures with loosely coupled components and serverless event-driven patterns.
common_confusions: Confusing Reliability (recovering from disruptions) with Performance Efficiency (using resources efficiently).
Forgetting Sustainability as the official sixth pillar of the Well-Architected Framework.
Treating Well-Architected design principles as strict audit requirements rather than architectural guidance.

tasks.name: Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud.

topics.name: AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)
Cloud Migration Strategies (7 Rs) & Migration Tools

selection_rules: Apply the 6 AWS CAF perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations.
Distinguish the 7 Rs of migration: Rehost (lift-and-shift), Replatform (lift-tinker-and-shift), Repurchase (drop-and-shop to SaaS), Refactor/Re-architect, Retain, Retire, Relocate.
Choose Rehost for urgent datacentre evacuation; choose Refactor to take full advantage of cloud-native serverless capabilities.
common_confusions: Confusing Rehosting (direct VM migration without code changes) with Replatforming (small optimizations like moving to managed RDS).
Confusing the Business perspective with the Governance perspective in AWS CAF.
Assuming migration always requires complete re-architecting on day one.

tasks.name: Understand concepts of cloud economics.

topics.name: Capital Expenditures (CapEx) vs Operational Expenditures (OpEx)
Economies of Scale, Rightsizing & Licensing (BYOL)

selection_rules: Trade upfront capital expense (CapEx datacenter hardware) for variable operational expense (OpEx pay-as-you-go).
Benefit from massive economies of scale passed along as frequent price reductions by AWS.
Apply continuous rightsizing to eliminate idle over-provisioned capacity before purchasing commitments.
common_confusions: Assuming cloud total cost of ownership (TCO) accounts only for direct server costs without facility and power savings.
Purchasing reservations before rightsizing workloads.
Confusing BYOL (Bring Your Own License) model with license-included compute instances.

tasks.name: Understand the AWS shared responsibility model.

topics.name: AWS Shared Responsibility Model: Customer vs AWS Duties
Responsibility Shifts: IaaS (EC2) vs PaaS (RDS) vs Serverless (Lambda)

selection_rules: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (hardware, physical datacenters, facilities, virtualization, network infrastructure).
Customer is responsible for security IN the cloud (customer data, IAM, OS patching on EC2, network firewall configuration, encryption).
As services move from IaaS (EC2) to managed PaaS (RDS) to serverless (Lambda), AWS assumes more patching and OS maintenance responsibility.
common_confusions: Assuming AWS patches the guest OS of Amazon EC2 instances.
Assuming the customer manages physical security or hardware decommissioning.
Believing managed database services (RDS) eliminate customer responsibility for data access controls.

tasks.name: Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts.

topics.name: AWS Artifact & Compliance Programs
Security Monitoring: GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub & Shield
Encryption (At Rest & In Transit) & Auditing (CloudTrail, Config)

selection_rules: Use AWS Artifact to access on-demand compliance reports (SOC, PCI-DSS, ISO) and agreements (BAA).
Select Amazon GuardDuty for intelligent threat detection; select Amazon Inspector for automated vulnerability scanning.
Use AWS CloudTrail for recording governance API activity and AWS Config for evaluating configuration compliance over time.
common_confusions: Confusing CloudTrail (who did what and when) with CloudWatch (performance metrics and logging).
Confusing Inspector (vulnerability scans on EC2/ECR) with GuardDuty (threat detection analyzing DNS, VPC, and CloudTrail logs).
Assuming encryption at rest in S3 also encrypts data during network transmission without TLS.

tasks.name: Identify AWS access management capabilities.

topics.name: IAM Users, Groups, Roles, Policies & Least Privilege
Root User Safeguards, MFA & Credential Hygiene
AWS IAM Identity Center & Identity Federation

selection_rules: Enforce least privilege: grant only the minimum necessary permissions required to perform a task.
Protect the AWS root user with multi-factor authentication (MFA), delete root access keys, and never use root for daily tasks.
Prefer IAM roles over long-term access keys for granting applications and AWS services temporary credentials.
Use AWS IAM Identity Center for centralized workforce single sign-on (SSO) and multi-account access.
common_confusions: Using root account credentials for daily administrative activities.
Embedding long-lived access keys in code instead of assigning IAM roles to EC2/Lambda.
Confusing IAM groups (containers of users for permission attachment) with IAM roles (assumable entities).

tasks.name: Identify components and resources for security.

topics.name: AWS WAF, Shield, Firewall Manager & Network Security
AWS Trusted Advisor, Security Center & AWS Marketplace Security

selection_rules: Deploy AWS WAF to protect web applications against common HTTP exploits (SQL injection, cross-site scripting).
Rely on AWS Shield Standard for automatic DDoS protection; upgrade to Shield Advanced for dedicated response team and financial protection.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor security checks to identify open security groups and missing MFA on the root account.
common_confusions: Confusing AWS WAF (Layer 7 web application firewall) with AWS Shield (Layer 3/4 DDoS protection).
Assuming AWS Shield Standard requires manual activation (it is enabled automatically at no extra charge).
Confusing Security Groups (stateful instance firewalls) with Network ACLs (stateless subnet firewalls).

tasks.name: Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud.

topics.name: Management Console, CLI, SDKs & Infrastructure as Code (CloudFormation)
Cloud, Hybrid & On-Premises Deployment Models

selection_rules: Use AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK for repeatable, automated Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
Choose programmatic access (AWS CLI / SDK) for automation and scripted deployments; use Console for ad-hoc visual management.
Distinguish deployment models: All-in Cloud (fully cloud-native), Hybrid (connecting on-premises datacenter with AWS), On-Premises/Private Cloud.
common_confusions: Confusing AWS CLI (command line execution) with AWS SDK (programming language libraries).
Using manual console click-paths for repeatable production deployments instead of IaC.
Assuming hybrid deployment means running two identical cloud providers simultaneously.

tasks.name: Define the AWS global infrastructure.

topics.name: AWS Regions, Availability Zones & High Availability
Edge Locations, Points of Presence & CloudFront/Global Accelerator
Multi-Region Deployments for Disaster Recovery & Latency

selection_rules: An AWS Region consists of three or more physically isolated, redundant Availability Zones (AZs).
An Availability Zone comprises one or more discrete datacenters with redundant power, networking, and connectivity.
Deploy workloads across multiple AZs within a Region for high availability and fault tolerance.
Use Edge Locations with Amazon CloudFront (CDN) to cache content closer to end users and reduce delivery latency.
common_confusions: Thinking an Availability Zone is a single data center building.
Confusing an Edge Location (content caching and DDoS mitigation) with a full AWS Region.
Assuming resources in different Regions communicate over public unencrypted links by default.

tasks.name: Identify AWS compute services.

topics.name: Amazon EC2 Instance Types & Use Cases
Container Options: Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS & AWS Fargate
Serverless Compute: AWS Lambda & Event-Driven Execution
Auto Scaling & Elastic Load Balancing

selection_rules: Select Amazon EC2 when complete OS-level control and custom software installations are required.
Choose AWS Lambda for serverless, event-driven execution with millisecond scaling and zero infrastructure management.
Use AWS Fargate to run containers serverlessly without managing EC2 host instances.
Pair Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to achieve elasticity and high availability under variable load.
common_confusions: Paying for idle server capacity with EC2 instead of choosing serverless Lambda for sporadic execution.
Confusing Amazon ECS (AWS native container orchestrator) with Amazon EKS (managed Kubernetes).
Confusing Elastic Load Balancing (traffic distribution) with Auto Scaling (instance capacity adjustment).

tasks.name: Identify AWS database services.

topics.name: Relational Databases: Amazon RDS & Amazon Aurora
NoSQL Databases: Amazon DynamoDB
In-Memory Caching: Amazon ElastiCache & MemoryDB
Database Migration: AWS DMS & AWS SCT

selection_rules: Choose Amazon RDS for traditional relational OLTP workloads (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server).
Choose Amazon Aurora for high-performance cloud-native MySQL/PostgreSQL with automatic multi-AZ 6-way replication.
Select Amazon DynamoDB for fully managed serverless key-value/document NoSQL with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale.
Use Amazon ElastiCache (Redis/Memcached) for in-memory caching to reduce database read pressure.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with minimal downtime during database transitions.
common_confusions: Choosing Amazon Redshift (OLAP data warehouse) for high-frequency transactional OLTP queries.
Hosting relational databases manually on EC2 without considering managed RDS automated backups and failover.
Confusing AWS DMS (data replication engine) with AWS SCT (schema conversion tool).

tasks.name: Identify AWS network services.

topics.name: Amazon VPC, Subnets, Route Tables & Gateways (IGW, NAT)
Security Groups vs Stateless Network ACLs
Amazon Route 53, AWS VPN & AWS Direct Connect

selection_rules: Provision isolated virtual networks with Amazon VPC, using public subnets for internet-facing assets and private subnets for backends.
Attach an Internet Gateway (IGW) for public routing and a NAT Gateway to allow private subnet instances outbound internet access.
Use Amazon Route 53 for scalable DNS resolution, domain registration, and health-check routing.
Choose AWS Direct Connect for a dedicated private fiber link; use AWS Site-to-Site VPN for quick encrypted IPsec tunnels over the internet.
common_confusions: Placing databases in public subnets instead of private subnets behind security groups.
Confusing stateful Security Groups (return traffic automatically allowed) with stateless Network ACLs (both directions must be explicitly permitted).
Assuming AWS Direct Connect automatically encrypts traffic without an overlay IPsec VPN.

tasks.name: Identify AWS storage services.

topics.name: Amazon S3 Storage Classes & Lifecycle Policies
Amazon EBS Volumes & EC2 Instance Store
File Systems: Amazon EFS & Amazon FSx
AWS Storage Gateway & AWS Backup

selection_rules: Choose Amazon S3 for durable object storage; use S3 Lifecycle policies to transition data to Glacier for low-cost archiving.
Use Amazon EBS for persistent block storage attached to a single EC2 instance.
Use EC2 Instance Store only for ephemeral temporary scratch data that does not require persistence across instance stop/termination.
Choose Amazon EFS for managed POSIX network file systems shareable concurrently across hundreds of Linux instances.
Use AWS Backup to centralize and automate data protection across AWS storage and database services.
common_confusions: Assuming EC2 instance store data persists when an instance is stopped (it is ephemeral and lost).
Confusing Amazon EBS (block storage attached to one instance) with Amazon EFS (network file storage shared by many).
Storing relational database data directly in S3 objects.

tasks.name: Identify AWS artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) services and analytics services.

topics.name: AI/ML Services: Amazon SageMaker AI, Bedrock, Lex, Polly, Rekognition
Analytics: Amazon Athena, EMR, AWS Glue, Kinesis & QuickSight

selection_rules: Use Amazon SageMaker AI to build, train, and deploy custom ML models at scale.
Use Amazon Bedrock to consume foundation models via serverless APIs for generative AI applications.
Use Amazon Athena to run interactive SQL queries directly against data files stored in Amazon S3 without loading servers.
Use AWS Glue for serverless ETL (extract, transform, load) and data cataloging; use Amazon QuickSight for business intelligence dashboards.
common_confusions: Deploying EMR clusters when simple ad-hoc SQL queries in S3 can be handled serverlessly by Athena.
Confusing Amazon Kinesis (streaming real-time data) with AWS Glue (batch ETL data preparation).
Confusing SageMaker (custom ML pipeline platform) with turn-key managed AI services like Rekognition.

tasks.name: Identify services from other in-scope AWS service categories.

topics.name: Messaging: Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge & Step Functions
Developer Tools: AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild & AWS X-Ray
End-User Computing (WorkSpaces, AppStream) & AWS IoT Core

selection_rules: Use Amazon SQS (message queues) to decouple asynchronous producers and consumers with durable buffering.
Use Amazon SNS (publish/subscribe) to fan out single messages to multiple subscribers (email, SMS, Lambda, SQS).
Use Amazon EventBridge to route events from AWS services and SaaS partners to targets using rules.
Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate complex multi-step distributed workflows and state machines.
Use Amazon WorkSpaces for secure, managed virtual cloud desktops accessible on any device.
common_confusions: Confusing SQS (one-to-one queue polling) with SNS (one-to-many topic fanout).
Confusing AWS CodeBuild (compiling source and running tests) with AWS CodeDeploy (automating deployment to targets).
Using custom polling scripts instead of native EventBridge event routing.

tasks.name: Compare AWS pricing models.

topics.name: Purchasing Options: On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Spot & Savings Plans
Data Transfer Pricing & Storage Tier Economics

selection_rules: Choose On-Demand Instances for short-term, unpredictable workloads without upfront commitment.
Choose Reserved Instances or Compute Savings Plans (1 or 3-year commitment) for predictable, steady-state workloads for up to 72% discounts.
Choose Spot Instances (up to 90% discount) for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads that can withstand interruptions.
Inbound data transfer to AWS is free; outbound data transfer across Regions or to the internet incurs egress costs.
common_confusions: Using Spot Instances for mission-critical, interruption-sensitive production workloads.
Assuming data transfer between EC2 instances in different AZs is always free.
Confusing EC2 Instance Savings Plans (commitment to a specific family in a region) with Compute Savings Plans (flexible across families, regions, and Fargate/Lambda).

tasks.name: Understand resources for billing, budget, and cost management.

topics.name: AWS Budgets, Cost Explorer & Cost and Usage Report (CUR)
AWS Pricing Calculator & Cost Estimation
AWS Organizations Consolidated Billing & Cost Allocation Tags

selection_rules: Use AWS Pricing Calculator to estimate monthly architecture costs prior to deploying workloads.
Use AWS Cost Explorer to visualize, understand, and forecast historical and future cloud spending patterns.
Configure AWS Budgets to set custom cost or usage thresholds and receive automated alerts via SNS or email before exceeding budgets.
Use AWS Organizations consolidated billing to combine usage across member accounts and qualify for volume pricing discounts.
Apply cost allocation tags to categorize resources by department, environment, or project for billing attribution.
common_confusions: Confusing Cost Explorer (historical visual analysis & forecasting) with AWS Budgets (proactive threshold alerts).
Confusing AWS Pricing Calculator (pre-deployment estimates) with AWS Cost and Usage Report (post-consumption granular data).
Expecting untagged resources to be automatically attributed to specific cost centers.

tasks.name: Identify AWS technical resources and AWS Support options.

topics.name: AWS Support Tiers: Basic, Developer, Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, Enterprise
AWS Trusted Advisor, AWS Health Dashboard & Documentation
AWS Partner Network (APN), Marketplace & Professional Services

selection_rules: Basic Support: 24x7 access to customer service, documentation, and 7 core Trusted Advisor checks at no charge.
Developer Support: Business hours email access to Cloud Support Associates, 1 primary contact, <12 hr general response.
Business Support: 24x7 phone, chat, and email access to Cloud Support Engineers, unlimited contacts, <1 hr production down response, full Trusted Advisor checks.
Enterprise Support: <15 min business-critical response, designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), Concierge team, Infrastructure Event Management (IEM).
Use AWS Health Dashboard for alerts on service degradations and planned maintenance impacting specific account resources.
common_confusions: Expecting phone or chat support with the Developer Support plan (it is email-only during business hours).
Expecting a dedicated TAM (Technical Account Manager) on the Business plan (requires Enterprise or Enterprise On-Ramp Support).
Confusing AWS Service Health Dashboard (public status of all AWS services) with AWS Personal Health Dashboard (account-specific impacts).
